summary: Weekly co-sell/pipeline sync with Avalon Partners to align on top joint opportunities, technical risk for AP-342 POC, and co-marketing motion. Main asks: benchmark for latency/cost, SSO/KMS requirements for Acme Foods, and an updated pipeline spreadsheet with commit dates.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-16
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Rao (Redwood); Ethan Park, Linda Huang, Marcus Bell (Avalon)

Auto-summary: quick run through of partner-sourced deals, action items to get POC underway for AP-342, discussion about dedicated vs hosted options and security requirements from Acme Foods, and next steps for joint GTM doc.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour so we'll run through the pipeline, focus on the Acme Foods opportunity and the POC ask from Marcus, and wrap with action items.
00:18 - Ethan Park: Great, thanks Maya, yeah we wanted to make sure we align on timelines — CFO is pushing for Q1 procurement window so -- so timing is a little tight.
00:34 - Linda Huang: Hi all, quick background, Avlon, sorry Avalon, our sales rep for Acme is already in final discovery, they really care about inference latency for customer-facing chat and cost per 1k requests.
00:47 - Diego Alvarez: Cool, Diego from Redwood here, I'm the solutions eng, happy to talk throughput/latency. One thing we usually do is try to size expected tokens per convo, that lets us pick Dedicated vs Hosted or a mixed routing.
01:05 - Marcus Bell: We have some regulatory constraints, Acme wants data not leaving their VPC, and they'd like KMS integration. Is Private deploy an option? Could be air gap but maybe VPC peering is fine.
01:27 - Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS is available, we have a on-prem and VPC option. Note, sometimes the naming in our docs says "Redwood Dedicate" in a few older decks, sorry typo, but it's the same Dedicated product.
01:45 - Ethan Park: Nice. For Acme the big tradeoff is cost: if we go full Private/on-prem it bumps licensing and infra... they asked about a hybrid route where the model runs in Avalon-managed region but logs and keys stay with Acme.
02:10 - Diego Alvarez: That hybrid routing is feasible with our routing policies; we can keep KV cache and keys local and route to hosted for burst. There is some nuance in throughput guarantees if you go hybrid.
02:30 - Speaker 1: (inaudible)
02:42 - Linda Huang: Question on benchmarks — can Redwood run a benchmark with Acme sample payloads? We need p50/p95 latency numbers and token costs to present.
02:55 - Diego Alvarez: Totally. I can run a bench, we'll need sample prompts and expected concurrency. I can also share a benchmark template.
03:10 - Maya Chen: We'll add that to action items. On pricing, we typically present tiered usage + dedicated commit for SLA, I'll send a Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison.
03:28 - Marcus Bell: Is there a standard SOC2/ISO attestation for Redwood? Acme's security team will want to see SOC/ISO and audit logs.
03:42 - Priya Rao: We are SOC2 Type II, and we can provide audit log samples. For Private deployments, extra controls and KMS/HSM integration are available.
03:55 - Ethan Park: Good, please share the security pack. Also SSO/SAML integration — Acme uses Okta.
04:10 - Diego Alvarez: Okta SSO is supported, RBAC and SCIM are possible. There is a small setup lead time but it's standard.
04:25 - Linda Huang: On the POC approach, would a short 2-week POC be enough to validate latency and quality?
04:35 - Maya Chen: Usually we propose a 3-week POC: week 1 onboarding and infra, week 2 benchmark and sample integration, week 3 tuning and executive review. But we can compress to 2 weeks if execs are aligned.
04:52 - Ethan Park: They'd push for 2 weeks ideally.
05:00 - Diego Alvarez: If you can give us sample traffic and a list of success metrics (p95 < 400ms, per token cost target) we can try 2 weeks.
05:20 - Marcus Bell: Success metrics: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 450ms, and monthly spend under $15k for the initial pilot. Also need logging to satisfy retention 12 months.
05:45 - Maya Chen: Ok noted. We'll map that into the POC scope.
06:01 - Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
06:10 - Linda Huang: On go-to-market, Avalon wants joint logos and a case study. Can Redwood do a co-branded playbook?
06:22 - Priya Rao: Yes, Partnerships can put together a joint GTM one-pager and co-sell assets. We'll also propose an exec intro to Acme.
06:38 - Ethan Park: For pipeline, top deals we flagged: AP-342 (Acme Foods) — $350k ARR potential; AP-289 (Greenfield Retail) — $120k; AP-410 (Nimbus Logistics) — $90k. AP-342 is priority.
06:58 - Diego Alvarez: For AP-342, what stage is that in Avalon CRM?
07:05 - Ethan Park: It's in 'proposal/negotiation' but needs security sign-off. Buyer persona is CIO + Head of Product.
07:18 - Maya Chen: Who's owning the technical conversations on Acme's side?
07:23 - Marcus Bell: That's me and their infra lead Samir. I'll share contacts.
07:30 - Diego Alvarez: Perfect. I'll reach out to Samir to get sample queries and run the benchmark. Could be helpful to know typical sequence lengths.
07:45 - Speaker 3: um-hm
07:52 - Linda Huang: We wanted to understand a little more about Redwood's batching and caching, we heard about KV cache but want example numbers for cost reduction.
08:04 - Diego Alvarez: Right, so our runtime does automatic prefix/KV caching and can reduce token cost significantly for repeated prompts — in some retail flows we've seen 30-45% token savings. It depends on repetition and statefulness. We can run a simulation for Acme flows.
08:26 - Ethan Park: That would be useful - can we see an example ROI calc?
08:30 - Maya Chen: We'll include a sample ROI table in the pipeline spreadsheet.
08:36 - Marcus Bell: A couple of technical constraints: Acme uses 512 token max per convo, high concurrency at peak times, and strict PII redaction rules.
08:50 - Diego Alvarez: We can set up a PII redaction layer, and we have labeling hooks. For 512 tokens that's within normal range; kernel selection will change with sequence length but should be fine.
09:04 - Linda Huang: Another question — we'd like to avoid long procurement; is there a partner discount or partner-managed invoice flow?
09:12 - Maya Chen: We have partner referral discounts and channel-managed invoicing available for Avalon partners — we can share the partner pricing addendum.
09:24 - Ethan Park: Good. For the Acme POC we need to present a combined cost plan.
09:31 - Diego Alvarez: I'll model both Hosted and Dedicated options and show where Dedicated pays off with commitments.
09:39 - Speaker 2: (murmur)
09:46 - Maya Chen: Quick note, competitors mentioned by Acme in their RFP were Anthropic and OpenAI— they asked about model comparatives and hallucination rates.
09:58 - Marcus Bell: Right, they want demonstration on retrieval-augmented generation for product catalog accuracy.
10:08 - Diego Alvarez: We have a demo harness for RAG + vector DB integrations; I can spin up a sample that uses their product catalog to show relevance numbers.
10:20 - Linda Huang: Timeline question — if we start POC next week can we have results by Thanksgiving week?
10:30 - Maya Chen: Thanksgiving is Nov 26 this year; compressed timeline is possible but we need full access to sample data and Samir's time.
10:42 - Ethan Park: I'll push to expedite.
10:48 - Marcus Bell: Also systems integration: they want to validate SSO and service account permissions. Samir will need doc on required ports and IAM roles.
10:58 - Diego Alvarez: I'll prepare a tech checklist and a minimal infra diagram.
11:10 - Speaker 1: (typing noises)
11:20 - Priya Rao: On co-marketing: Avalon suggested a joint webinar targeting retail clients. We can draft a co-host abstract.
11:31 - Linda Huang: Yes let's do a webinar, maybe early Jan after POC success.
11:38 - Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll propose dates after POC.
11:44 - Ethan Park: For reporting, can Redwood provide token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency? That'll help Acme's finance team.
11:55 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, our Console exposes token-level cost & latency, and we can provide a temporary access or export for the POC window.
12:07 - Marcus Bell: One more item — encryption at rest and transit, and key rotation policies.
12:14 - Priya Rao: KMS integrations support rotation policies, HSM is available for Private. We'll include the security docs in the pack.
12:28 - Speaker 2: (low audio)
12:36 - Maya Chen: Ok, let's summarize action items quickly: Diego runs benchmark and shares template; Maya sends pricing + Hosted vs Dedicated comparison; Priya sends security pack; Ethan shares contacts and sample payloads. Anything else?
12:55 - Ethan Park: I'll share the Acme procurement timeline and buyer contacts.
13:03 - Linda Huang: I'll coordinate webinar logistics after POC.
13:10 - Marcus Bell: I'll intro Samir to Diego and provide the sample queries.
13:18 - Maya Chen: Great. Next meeting — propose 11/23 10am PST for a short status check.
13:27 - Ethan Park: That works.
13:33 - Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, adjourn.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional audio drop and a couple of misheard product names (eg Redwood Dedicated -> "Redwood Dedicate"). Speaker labels are mostly correct; some crosstalk present.
